clue.text: With some hesitation I lay claim to this emblem of honour

parts.note: the sound of a speaker hesitating
what you say when claiming something: it's mine

explanation.surface: A modest recipient hesitantly claims a decoration as their own.
explanation.walkthrough: Ermine is the white winter fur of the stoat, used to trim the robes of peers and judges.
explanation.definitionFit: The fur trimming on ceremonial robes of peers marks rank and dignity, so it stands as a badge of honour.

clue.text: Charm is not way-out

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to delight or bewitch, stressed on the second syllable
second meaning: the way in rather than the exit

explanation.walkthrough: 'Way-out' looks like slang for eccentric, but it is the exit, and the opposite is the way in.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to enchant or captivate; as a noun it is the door through which you come in.

clue.text: Drink rifled by Henry?

parts.note: surface reading: a drink stolen by someone called Henry
setter's reading: the name of a Victorian army rifle that was coupled with Henry's name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rifled' looks like plundered, but it points to the Martini-Henry, a British army rifle combining Martini's breech and Henry's barrel rifling. The same name is a vermouth and a gin cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocktail of gin and vermouth shares its name with the gun designer whose breech went with Henry's barrel.

clue.text: A convenient amount for the eye to take in

definitions.text: A convenient amount for the eye to take in

parts.words: A convenient amount for the eye to take in
parts.note: surface reading: a manageable amount to look at
setter's reading: the eye of a sewing needle, taking in a length of thread

explanation.walkthrough: 'Eye' and 'take in' suggest looking, but the eye is the hole a thread passes through.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the length of thread cut for sewing, enough to be threaded and worked comfortably at once.

clue.text: Puce is so awfully showy

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, so the letters come out of order

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A fashion critic sneers that a purplish-brown outfit is terribly loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Specious means superficially attractive but hollow, all outward show without substance underneath.

clue.text: Pedestrian in a right mess, and he knows he is fated

indicators.note: things in a mess are jumbled, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, part of the fodder
taken as written, part of the fodder
abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A walker caught in a muddle accepts that his fate is sealed.
explanation.definitionFit: A believer in predestination holds that everything, including salvation, is decided beforehand by God.

clue.text: Bell may thus sound a tribal note

parts.note: a clan is a tribal group
one of the musical notes A to G

explanation.surface: A bell rings out a note belonging to a tribe.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud ringing metallic noise is exactly how a struck bell is heard.

clue.text: No gun firm rises to this figure

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
old American slang for a pistol
abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: No arms company reaches this sales figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' suggests a number, but it is a geometric shape.
explanation.definitionFit: An eight-sided polygon is a shape in geometry, a plane figure.

clue.text: Goodfellow didn't walk? Yes, he did

definitions.note: answers the question: he did walk, in a stride

parts.note: a good fellow is a saint, abbreviated
he went on horseback instead of walking

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether Robin Goodfellow went on foot, and is told he did.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue looks like a name and question, but the saint and the riding build the word, and the reply 'Yes, he did' means he walked with long steps.
explanation.definitionFit: The reply affirms that he walked, and the past tense of stride describes walking with long purposeful steps.

clue.text: Creation of new compound for post office by troubled military zone

parts.note: the standard abbreviation for post office; 'for' leads it in

indicators.note: something troubled is disturbed, so its letters are stirred up

parts.note: the twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A new branch building planned for a post office lies in a disputed army area.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry, small molecules linking into long chains make a new substance, a polymer.

clue.text: This game of course is partly one-sided

definitions.text: This game of course is partly one-sided

parts.words: This game of course is partly one-sided
parts.note: surface reading: a match that is naturally a bit lopsided
setter's reading: a game on a golf course where one side has a single player

explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' sounds like 'naturally', but it means on a golf course. In this golf format one player takes on a pair, so one of the two sides is a single person.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf this format pits a lone player against a partnership, so one side of the match has just one player.

clue.text: Table for a trainee sailor

parts.note: taken as written
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
a tar is an old word for a seaman

explanation.surface: A seating arrangement or bench meant for a young naval recruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The communion table in a church, or any raised table for offerings, is this sacred piece of furniture.

clue.text: A team to combine round the centre line

parts.note: taken as written
eleven in Roman numerals, a cricket or football side
to ally is to join forces

explanation.surface: A sports squad is told to group together around the halfway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre line' sounds like a pitch marking, but the definition means turning about an axis.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arranged or rotating about an axis, the central line of a body, is placed in this manner.

clue.text: Started to fight in glove in scrap

indicators.note: one item sits inside the other, so the glove word goes within the scrap word

parts.note: a scrap or remnant, as in a fag-end; it holds the next piece
a gage was a glove thrown down as a challenge to fight

explanation.surface: A boxer started fighting while wearing a glove, in a scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a fight, matching the surface, but it is a leftover bit.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops who have engaged the enemy have begun combat with them, entering battle.

clue.text: The highest cardinal

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the top person or most important
second meaning: as an adjective, principal or main, as in cardinal points

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a prince of the Church, but here it is the adjective meaning principal.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the leader or top person, and as an adjective it means principal or most important.

clue.text: Alluring new net is topping

indicators.note: something new is remade, so the following letters take a fresh order

parts.note: the three letters to be rearranged
the sweet coating on a cake

explanation.surface: Someone admires a fresh net curtain as excellent and attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' looks like old slang for excellent, but it is the cake coating.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enticing tempts and attracts, which is just what alluring means.

clue.text: One location arranged for the wartime government

indicators.note: arranged means put into a set order, here a new order of letters

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written, part of the fodder

explanation.surface: A single site is set up for the government during the war.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain was governed in the Second World War by a cross-party alliance under Churchill, a joint ministry.

clue.text: Cradle singers' catch

parts.note: Italian plural of basso, deep male singers
to net is to catch

explanation.surface: A lullaby round sung by people at a baby's crib.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch' suggests a round sung by several singers, but it means to trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A bassinet is a hooded basket or crib in which a baby sleeps.

clue.text: Boy's about to choose one kitchen worker

indicators.note: going about something means surrounding it, so the boy's word wraps the rest

parts.note: a boy is a son; the 's means 'is', and this word surrounds the rest
to cull is to pick out or select
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lad is about to pick one cook's helper.
explanation.definitionFit: A scullion was a lowly servant who did the rough work in a kitchen, such as washing pots.

clue.text: Australian left in the drink

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside it, so the side goes within the Australian word

parts.note: Australian slang for a mate or friend; it holds the next piece
abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: An Australian has been abandoned in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The drink' looks like slang for the sea, but it is a real drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler is an iced cocktail of wine or sherry with sugar and fruit.

clue.text: Expression of surprise after a record beginning

indicators.note: coming after something means standing behind it, so the exclamation is placed last

parts.note: taken as written
a long-playing record
an exclamation of surprise; 'after' puts it behind the record

explanation.surface: Someone gasps when a record-breaking run gets under way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the exclamation behind the other pieces. As in 'alpha and omega', the first Greek letter stands for the beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: The first letter of the Greek alphabet stands for the start of anything, as in alpha and omega.

clue.text: Undertaking to show the way in plain speech

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside it, so the way goes within the speech

parts.note: ordinary writing or speech, not verse; it holds the next piece
the M1, Britain's main motorway, written with an I

explanation.surface: A pledge to guide people, given in simple words.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; crosswords write it MI.
explanation.definitionFit: A promise is a pledge or vow, an undertaking to do something.

clue.text: Small comfort for objectionable people?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: tiny bits of consolation
second meaning: slang for contemptible or worthless persons

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests little sympathy for nasty people; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means scraps, as in crumbs of comfort, and is old slang for despicable people.

clue.text: Costume right with a film musical

parts.note: a robe is a garment or costume
a standard abbreviation of right
taken as written

explanation.surface: A costume designer gets things right for a movie musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Roberta is a 1935 Hollywood musical with Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers, based on a Jerome Kern stage show.

clue.text: Greek's letter to doctor for a lozenge

parts.note: the Greek letter R
Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A Greek patient writes to the doctor asking for a throat sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lozenge' suggests a cough sweet, but it is the diamond shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A lozenge is a diamond-shaped figure, an equilateral parallelogram, which is what a rhomb is.

clue.text: Football ace with common sense is devastating

parts.note: Rugby Union, a code of football
an ace is a one, written as I
British word for practical good sense

explanation.surface: A star footballer with brains is unstoppable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Football ace' reads as a star player, but it splits into the code and a one. Nous is everyday British for gumption.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ruinous brings ruin, wrecking or destroying whatever it touches.

clue.text: Very low about the officer

indicators.note: going about something means surrounding it, so the low word wraps the officer

parts.note: to low is to make a cow's sound; it surrounds the next piece
abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: Morale is very low around the officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb for what a cow does. Molto is the Italian musical direction.
explanation.definitionFit: In musical directions the Italian word means much or greatly, as in molto allegro.

clue.text: I race around N. Ireland in state of exhaustion

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: going around something means enclosing it, so the race word wraps the province

parts.note: a race or people; it is split to hold the next piece
the usual abbreviation for Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A cyclist or runner tours Northern Ireland and ends up worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Race' reads as a contest, but it is a people.
explanation.definitionFit: Inanition is weakness and emptiness caused by lack of nourishment, an exhausted condition.

clue.text: Dance girl accompanied by a group

parts.note: a girl's name
a band is a group of musicians or people

explanation.surface: A dancing girl performs with a backing band.
explanation.definitionFit: The saraband is a slow stately Spanish dance in triple time, often found in baroque suites.

clue.text: Undercover purpose

explanation.walkthrough: 'Undercover' suggests spying, but read literally it is sheltered inside a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: An intent is an aim or design, what someone means to do.
